newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL TO RAISE $45 BLN WITH POWER SELLOFFS-REPORT.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL TO RAISE $45 BLN WITH POWER SELLOFFS-REPORT.

text.p: Brazil expects to raise at least $45 billion by 1999 with the upcoming privatizations of its power companies, Gazeta Mercantil financial newspaper said on Wednesday.

Jose Pio Borges, vice-president of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), told the paper just the assets of the three Sao Paulo state electrical firms -- Cesp, Eletropaulo and Companhia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL) -- together represent $18 billion.
The generating units of federal power holding Eletrobras -- Furnas, Eletrosul, Eletronorte and CHESF -- may provide 21.3 billion reais (about $19.5 billion) to the Brazilian government, he added.
BNDES oversees most of Brazil's privatizations.

So far the privatization of the Brazilian electrical sector has resulted in 6.75 billion reais (about $6 billion) in revenues, Gazeta said. The companies already sold are Light, Escelsa, Cerj and Coelba, it added.
